questions.question: What do we learn about the current electric supply system in Africa?

options.A: It curbs the economic development of the continent.
options.B: It mainly depends on the polluting diesel generators.
options.C: It is the primary cause of inequitable distribution of wealth.
options.D: It deprives many Africans of the opportunity to use computers.

analysis.correct_reason: 原文第二段 'The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents' 直接说明现有供电系统压制了经济发展潜力，A选项 'curbs the economic development' 是对此的同义改写。

distractor_analysis.B: 过度概括：柴油发电机是临时解决方案，但文中未说现有系统'主要依赖'它。
distractor_analysis.C: 因果混淆：文中说的是电力不平等导致生计风险，没有说它是财富分配不平等的'首要原因'。
distractor_analysis.D: 范围过窄：Agok的电脑课只是一个具体例子，文章讨论的是更宏观的经济影响。

questions.difficulty_reason: 需要识别 'keeps a lid on' 的引申义，并区分具体例子和中心论点

questions.question: What do we learn from the passage about Africa's past electrification efforts?

options.A: They have failed to meet most Africans' need of a reliable power supply.
options.B: They have failed to build a national grid to provide electric power.
options.C: They have unleashed the true economic potential of the continent.
options.D: They have aimed at wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.

analysis.correct_reason: 原文第三段 'fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity'，说明政府主导的电气化努力未能满足大多数人的可靠供电需求。

distractor_analysis.B: 绝对化陷阱：并非未建成电网，而是电网不够可靠，'failed to build' 与原文不符。
distractor_analysis.C: 与原文相反：文章说的是现状未能释放经济潜力。
distractor_analysis.D: 混淆时态与主语：这是作者的建议，不是对过去努力的描述。

questions.difficulty_reason: 需要区分'未能建成电网'和'电网不可靠'的细微差别，B选项是常见陷阱

questions.question: What is essential to tackling the power supply shortage in Africa?

options.A: Replacing temporary solutions with long-term strategies.
options.B: Accelerating economic growth with sustainable policies.
options.D: Putting in place a large-scale modern power grid speedily.

analysis.correct_reason: 原文第四段末句 'Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential'，D选项是对这句话的同义改写：speed→speedily，at scale→large-scale。

distractor_analysis.A: 目的/手段混淆：'replacing temporary solutions' 是目标，D说的是实现手段；A缺少'速度'和'规模'这两个关键要素。
distractor_analysis.B: 无中生有：'sustainable policies' 文中没有对应表述。
distractor_analysis.C: 无中生有：文章完全未提及重组国有电力公司。

questions.difficulty_reason: 需要识别 'Deploying...with speed and at scale' 对应 D 中的 'speedily' 和 'large-scale'

questions.question: What are many governments in Africa doing to solve the electricity supply problem?

options.B: Relying on the private sector for scale economy.

analysis.correct_reason: 原文第五段 'many governments...have begun to embrace the private sector as partners'，D选项 'Cooperating with private companies' 是对 'embrace...as partners' 的准确改写。

distractor_analysis.A: 主语混淆：'building world-class infrastructure' 是私营企业做的事，不是政府。
distractor_analysis.B: 词义混淆：'scale economy（规模经济）' 是经济学术语，原文说的是 'at scale（大规模）'，含义不同。
distractor_analysis.C: 主语混淆：'sustainable business models' 是私营企业的特点，不是政府行为。

questions.difficulty_reason: A和C的陷阱在于混淆了行为主语（政府vs私营企业），是六级常见高难度干扰策略

questions.question: Why will private companies be motivated to join the effort of electrifying sub-Saharan Africa?

options.A: There is big money to be made.
options.B: They have enough funding in place.
options.C: South Africa has set a successful example.
options.D: Governments are turning to them for help.

analysis.correct_reason: 原文第七段 'electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity'，A选项 'big money to be made' 是对商业机会的口语化改写，指出了商业利润动机。

distractor_analysis.B: 条件/现实混淆：原文 'With the right funding in place' 是假设条件，并非说私企已有足够资金。
distractor_analysis.C: 混淆原因与例子：南非是说明私营模式可行的例子，不是私企参与的动机。
distractor_analysis.D: 混淆动机与结果：政府求助是现象，不是私企参与的根本原因。

questions.difficulty_reason: 需要将 '$350 billion opportunity' 推断为商业利润动机，属于轻度推理题

CET6-RC-202606-S3-P2.topic: 非洲电力供给与私营部门的作用
CET6-RC-202606-S3-P2.text:
On a warm October morning, Daniel Agok woke up to another disappointing day at his school in Wanyjok, South Sudan. The classes he had planned teaching computer skills to aspiring young professionals were canceled, due to an unreliable diesel generator and the absence of a municipal power grid in his area. Now, he would be losing frustrated customers as well as income. Agok is just one of the hundreds of millions of people in sub-Saharan Africa, many of whom are business owners, who still do not have dependable electricity. This inequitable access to energy continues to put their livelihood and future at risk.

The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students. We must instead unleash their abilities and let Africa reach its true economic potential. That means wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.

Historically, national governments on the continent have led electrification efforts, but fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity.

This has led to expensive and harmful temporary solutions. In Nigeria alone experts estimate people spend $13 billion every year on fuel for toxic, polluting generators. That number will only grow as the continent's population hits 2.5 billion people by 2050. Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions with reliable and affordable alternatives.

The rapidly growing private power sector in Africa holds the key to achieving the speed and scale necessary to close the continent's energy access gap. Private companies today are building world-class infrastructure and driving forward economic growth with sustainable business models. In fact, many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale. In South Africa, President Cyril Ramaphosa has streamlined licensing requirements and enlisted the private sector to play a key role.

South Africa is just one example. Across the continent, the private sector has delivered power faster and more reliably, and governments are increasingly turning to private partners.

With the right funding and structure in place, the private sector will come together to provide this essential service. After all, electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity.

Today, Daniel Agok is steadily growing his business in South Sudan. His town of Wanyjok was electrified by a private company, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to his business and his neighbors. Agok now operates his growing computer skills training business smoothly. His classes are no longer affected by the smell and the constant noise of the diesel generator, and he saves money with more affordable power. His students are developing hardware and software skills.
